units.explain: Module header of flask/app.py: imports stdlib modules (collections.abc, inspect, os, sys, typing, weakref, datetime, functools, itertools, types, urllib.parse), Werkzeug pieces (datastructures, exceptions, routing, serving, wrappers, wsgi), and intra-package imports from flask.cli, flask.typing, flask.ctx, flask.globals, flask.helpers, flask.sansio.app, flask.sessions, flask.signals, flask.templating, and flask.wrappers. A TYPE_CHECKING block imports WSGI types and testing classes for annotations only. TypeVars T_shell_context_processor, T_teardown, T_template_filter, T_template_global, T_template_test are bound to flask.typing callback protocols.
units.summary: Imports and TypeVar definitions for the concrete Flask application class.
uncertainties: Behavior of imported symbols is defined in their own modules, not here.

units.explain: Normalizes a cache-lifetime value to a timedelta or None. Returns None unchanged if value is None, returns value unchanged if it is already a timedelta, and otherwise interprets value as a number of seconds and returns timedelta(seconds=value). No side effects; no error handling for non-numeric values.
units.summary: Convert an int/None cache-lifetime value into a timedelta, passing through None and timedelta.
uncertainties: Callers of this helper are not visible in this file; its exact call sites are unproven here.

units.explain: Decorator supporting the deprecated pre-3.2 override signatures for Flask request-lifecycle methods. Wraps a subclass method that lacks the new ctx parameter: the wrapper drops a leading AppContext positional argument (when present) from the arguments supplied by the new-style base implementation, then calls the wrapped function with the remaining args/kwargs. update_wrapper copies __name__/__doc__ onto the wrapper. Side effect: the wrapper replaces the method on the subclass (done by __init_subclass__, not here).
units.summary: Decorator wrapping legacy Flask method overrides to strip the leading AppContext argument before calling them.
uncertainties: Non-AppContext first arguments are passed through unchanged; behavior when the caller passes something that is not an AppContext but is meant as ctx is undefined by this reading.

units.explain: Small residual region between _make_timedelta and remove_ctx defining the TypeVar F bound to a callable; F parameterizes the remove_ctx/add_ctx decorators. No executable behavior.
units.summary: TypeVar F definition used by the ctx-compatibility decorators.

units.explain: Residual region between add_ctx and the Flask class body; in the source it contains only the boundary between the add_ctx decorator and the class definition, no additional statements.
units.summary: Residual region preceding the Flask class definition.

units.explain: Counterpart to remove_ctx: wraps the Flask base implementation of the deprecated-signature methods so that when a subclass override calls super().method() with the old signature (no ctx), the base still receives an AppContext. The wrapper prepends app_ctx._get_current_object(): if no positional args are given it becomes the sole first argument; if the first positional arg is not an AppContext it is prepended before the existing args. Then calls f with the adjusted args. update_wrapper preserves metadata.
units.summary: Decorator wrapping Flask base methods to insert the current AppContext for legacy super() calls.
uncertainties: Behavior depends on the app_ctx context proxy having a current object at call time; behavior when no app context is active is not shown here.

units.explain: The concrete WSGI application class, subclassing the sansio App. It extends App with WSGI-specific behavior: request dispatch, error handling, response conversion, teardown, static file serving, Jinja environment creation, URL building, the dev server (run), and test helpers. Class-level state includes default_config (a Mapping of default configuration keys such as DEBUG, TESTING, PROPAGATE_EXCEPTIONS, SESSION_COOKIE_* values, SEND_FILE_MAX_AGE_DEFAULT, TRAP_HTTP_EXCEPTIONS, MAX_COOKIE_SIZE, etc.), request_class=Request, response_class=Response, and a class-level session_interface instance of SecureCookieSessionInterface (shared as a default). Instances are normally created as Flask(import_name) with optional static/template folder and instance-path configuration; __init__ adds the static route via a weakref to avoid a reference cycle and builds a cli.AppGroup named after the app. Methods marked in the inventory below handle lifecycle; the class as a unit covers its identity, inheritance from App, and class attributes. Methods with actual logic each get their own unit.
units.summary: Concrete Flask WSGI application class extending sansio.App with dispatch, error handling, static files, templating, and dev-server support.

relations.basis: __init__ calls self.add_url_rule for the static route

uncertainties: The sansio App base class and its attributes (config, url_map, jinja_options, etc.) are defined in another module; their behavior is not proven here.

units.explain: Runs when Flask is subclassed. Iterates the twelve lifecycle methods whose signatures gained an AppContext ctx parameter; for each, compares the subclass attribute with the Flask base. If overridden, inspects the second parameter (after self) and accepts it only if: no annotation and named 'ctx', a string annotation whose last dotted component is 'AppContext', or a class annotation that is a subclass of AppContext. Otherwise it emits a DeprecationWarning about Flask 4.0, sets the subclass attribute to remove_ctx(method) so old-style overrides still get called correctly, and mutates the Flask base method in place with add_ctx(base_method) so legacy super() calls still receive a ctx. Note: the Flask class attribute is mutated for any violating subclass, affecting the shared base; this is intended so the compatibility shims line up.
units.summary: Detects deprecated pre-3.2 override signatures in subclasses and wraps them with ctx-compatibility shims, warning via DeprecationWarning.
uncertainties: inspect.signature on decorated/bound attributes could raise for exotic overrides; not guarded here.

units.explain: Constructs the app. Delegates all parameter validation and basic state (root_path, config, url_map, static folder detection) to App.__init__ with the same keyword arguments. Then creates self.cli as a cli.AppGroup named after self.name, and, if the app has a static folder, registers the static route '<static_url_path>/<path:filename>' with endpoint 'static' and a view function that goes through a weakref to self (avoiding a reference cycle, per the cited issue). Asserts bool(static_host) == host_matching when a static folder exists, so a static_host without host_matching (or vice versa) raises AssertionError at construction. The static route is added without checking that the static folder exists on disk.
units.summary: Initialize the Flask app: create the CLI group and register the static-file route via a weakref-backed view.

extras.note: Asserts bool(static_host) == host_matching when a static folder is configured; mismatch raises AssertionError during construction.

uncertainties: Behavior inherited from App.__init__ (path resolution, config loading defaults) lives in flask/sansio/app.py and is not proven from this file.

units.explain: Resolves the cache max-age for a file path from config['SEND_FILE_MAX_AGE_DEFAULT']. Returns None if unset (meaning conditional requests instead of a timed cache), converts a timedelta to total whole seconds via int(total_seconds()), and returns any other value as-is. Pure lookup; no I/O.
units.summary: Return the SEND_FILE_MAX_AGE_DEFAULT config as int seconds or None.
uncertainties: The final untyped return assumes the config value is already an int when not None/timedelta; a bad config value would be returned unvalidated.

units.explain: View function serving files from static_folder. Raises RuntimeError if has_static_folder is false (i.e. static_folder not configured). Otherwise computes max_age via get_send_file_max_age and delegates to helpers.send_from_directory(self.static_folder, filename, max_age=max_age), inheriting its security and error behavior (404/404-style responses for missing files come from that helper).
units.summary: Static-file view: serve a file from static_folder via send_from_directory or raise if no static folder.

extras.note: Raises RuntimeError when 'static_folder' is not set, instead of returning a 404 response.

uncertainties: Exact error-response semantics (404 vs 403, traversal protection) are defined in helpers.send_from_directory, outside this file.

units.explain: Opens a file relative to root_path. Only read modes are permitted: mode must be one of 'r', 'rt', 'rb'; anything else raises ValueError('Resources can only be opened for reading.'). For binary mode, opens with built-in open(path, mode); for text modes, opens with the given encoding (default None means locale default). The file is returned as a regular file object usable with a with block; no automatic closing here. Paths are joined with os.path.join so absolute resource paths would escape root_path per os.path semantics.
units.summary: Open a read-only file relative to the app root_path, rejecting write modes.

extras.note: Raises ValueError for any mode other than 'r', 'rt', or 'rb'.

uncertainties: Whether absolute or '../'-containing resource values are rejected is not guarded; relies on os.path.join/open behavior.

units.explain: Opens a file relative to instance_path. Unlike open_resource, write modes are allowed. Binary modes (mode containing 'b') open without encoding; otherwise opens in text mode with encoding, defaulting to 'utf-8'. No existence or permission checks; OS errors propagate.
units.summary: Open a file relative to the instance folder, allowing write modes.

units.explain: Builds the Jinja Environment once, from self.jinja_options. Copies the options dict; fills in 'autoescape' with select_jinja_autoescape if absent, and 'auto_reload' with config['TEMPLATES_AUTO_RELOAD'] falling back to self.debug when that config is None. Instantiates self.jinja_environment(self, **options), then injects template globals: url_for (the method), get_flashed_messages, config, and the request/session/g proxies (the proxies are included so imported templates can access them). Sets the 'json.dumps_function' policy to self.json.dumps. Changing jinja_options after this runs has no effect because the environment is created from a snapshot.
units.summary: Create the Jinja Environment with autoescape/auto_reload defaults and Flask template globals.

relations.basis: url_for is exposed as a Jinja global

uncertainties: jinja_environment attribute and select_jinja_autoescape are defined on the sansio App; behavior of the returned Environment is defined in flask.templating.

units.explain: Creates the Werkzeug MapAdapter. With a request: assigns config['TRUSTED_HOSTS'] to request.trusted_hosts if set, normalizes request.host via werkzeug.wsgi.get_host against those trusted hosts, then computes server_name from config['SERVER_NAME'] — set to None when url_map.host_matching is enabled (so the real host is honored) — and computes subdomain: None when subdomain_matching is enabled, otherwise forced to url_map.default_subdomain or '' to disable subdomain matching. Binds via url_map.bind_to_environ(request.environ, server_name=..., subdomain=...). Without a request: returns url_map.bind(SERVER_NAME, script_name=APPLICATION_ROOT, url_scheme=PREFERRED_URL_SCHEME) if SERVER_NAME is configured, else None. bind_to_environ can raise for untrusted hosts per Werkzeug.
units.summary: Bind a Werkzeug URL map adapter for a request, or for app-only use when SERVER_NAME is set.

relations.basis: AppContext.__init__ calls this method to obtain the url_adapter

uncertainties: Exact exception behavior of bind_to_environ (e.g. host mismatch) is Werkzeug-defined, not shown here.

units.explain: Re-raises the request's routing_exception to the caller (which lets wsgi_app/ctx handle it as an HTTP exception). In debug mode only, a RequestRedirect that would discard a form body is intercepted: if the routing exception is a RequestRedirect whose code is not 307/308 and the request method is not GET/HEAD/OPTIONS, it raises debughelpers.FormDataRoutingRedirect(request) instead, giving a clearer error. 307/308 redirects and safe methods are always re-raised unchanged; non-RequestRedirect routing exceptions are re-raised unchanged. Always raises; returns NoReturn.
units.summary: Re-raise routing exceptions, converting body-discarding RequestRedirects to FormDataRoutingRedirect in debug mode.

relations.basis: raise FormDataRoutingRedirect(request) after a local import

uncertainties: Behavior when request.routing_exception is None (attribute typed via sansio) is not visible; the caller presumably never invokes it then.

units.explain: Mutates the given context dict in place with template context processors. Processor lookup names start with None (app-level) and, if the app context has a request, extend with the request's blueprints in reverse order (most specific first). For each name present in template_context_processors, each processor is invoked through ensure_sync and its returned dict merged. After all processors, the original context snapshot (values passed by the caller, e.g. render_template kwargs) is re-applied so explicit values win over processor values. No return value.
units.summary: Run template context processors and re-apply caller-provided context so explicit values take precedence.
uncertainties: Whether ctx.has_request/blueprints semantics include nested blueprints is defined by the request object, not here.

units.explain: Builds the interactive-shell namespace: starts from {'app': self, 'g': g} and updates with the dict returned by each registered shell context processor in registration order (later processors can override earlier keys, including 'app'/'g'). Returns the resulting dict.
units.summary: Return the shell namespace including app, g, and all shell context processor results.

units.explain: Development-only server launcher; documented as unsuitable for production. If FLASK_RUN_FROM_CLI is 'true', it prints a red warning (unless running under the reloader) and returns without starting a server. If load_dotenv resolves truthy (via helpers.get_load_dotenv, which also honors the FLASK_SKIP_DOTENV env var), cli.load_dotenv() loads .env/.flaskenv files; then if FLASK_DEBUG is set, self.debug is refreshed via helpers.get_debug_flag. An explicit debug argument overrides everything. Host/port defaults come from config['SERVER_NAME'] parsed with urlsplit('//SERVER_NAME'): host falls back to its hostname then '127.0.0.1'; port is int(port) when truthy or 0, else SERVER_NAME's port, else 5000. Werkzeug run_simple options default: use_reloader=debug, use_debugger=debug, threaded=True. Prints the server banner, imports werkzeug.serving.run_simple lazily, and blocks in run_simple(host, port, self, **options); the finally block resets self._got_first_request to False so the app can restart in an interactive session. Unknown **options are forwarded to run_simple and may raise there.
units.summary: Run the Werkzeug development server with debug/dotenv/SERVER_NAME defaults; ignore when started via 'flask run'.

extras.note: Mutates self.debug and self._got_first_request; loads dotenv files which may change the working directory.
Returns without starting a server when FLASK_RUN_FROM_CLI is 'true'.

uncertainties: run_simple's option handling and server behavior are Werkzeug-defined.

units.explain: Returns a test client instance: self.test_client_class if set, else a lazily imported flask.testing.FlaskClient. The client is constructed as cls(self, self.response_class, use_cookies=use_cookies, **kwargs), so extra kwargs are forwarded to the client constructor. Exceptions in app code are only visible to tests when app.testing (or debug) makes them propagate; otherwise they surface as 500 responses.
units.summary: Create a test client (custom class or default FlaskClient) bound to this app.
uncertainties: Constructor contract of FlaskClient is defined in flask.testing, not here.

units.explain: Returns self.test_cli_runner_class(self, **kwargs) if set, else a lazily imported flask.testing.FlaskCliRunner(self, **kwargs). The app is passed as the first constructor argument.
units.summary: Create a CLI test runner (custom class or default FlaskCliRunner) for this app.
uncertainties: FlaskCliRunner constructor semantics are defined in flask.testing.

units.explain: Handles an HTTPException raised during dispatch. Returns the exception unchanged when e.code is None (proxy-style exceptions without codes) or when it is a werkzeug RoutingException (internal control-flow like slash redirects, deliberately not routed to error handlers). Otherwise looks up an error handler via _find_error_handler(e, ctx.request.blueprints); if none is found, returns the exception itself (which becomes the error response); otherwise calls the handler through ensure_sync with the exception and returns its result.
units.summary: Handle HTTPExceptions: pass through code-less and routing exceptions, else dispatch to a registered error handler.
uncertainties: Handler return-value typing (ResponseReturnValue) is trusted; a handler returning an invalid value surfaces later in make_response.

units.explain: Entry point for exceptions raised in view/handler code. If the exception is a BadRequestKeyError and debug or TRAP_BAD_REQUEST_ERRORS is set, sets e.show_exception = True so the missing key is displayed. If the exception is an HTTPException and trap_http_exception(e) is False, forwards it to handle_http_exception(ctx, e). Otherwise, looks up a handler via _find_error_handler(e, ctx.request.blueprints); if none exists, re-raises the original exception (bare 'raise', preserving traceback); otherwise calls the handler through ensure_sync and returns its result.
units.summary: Convert or propagate user exceptions: HTTPExceptions go to handle_http_exception, other errors go to handlers or re-raise.

extras.note: Re-raises the original exception, preserving its traceback, when no error handler is registered.

units.explain: Last-resort handler for unhandled exceptions or exceptions raised in error handlers. Captures sys.exc_info(), sends the got_request_exception signal (with ensure_sync as the async wrapper). Determines propagate from config['PROPAGATE_EXCEPTIONS'], defaulting to (testing or debug) when None; if propagating, re-raises the active exception (bare raise when exc_info[1] is e) or raises e. Otherwise logs the exception via log_exception(ctx, exc_info), builds InternalServerError(original_exception=e), looks up a handler for it (handlers registered for InternalServerError/500 receive the InternalServerError, never the original), and returns finalize_request(ctx, server_error, from_error_handler=True), so after-request functions still run and failures in that path are logged rather than raised.
units.summary: Convert an unhandled exception into a 500 InternalServerError response, or re-raise when exceptions propagate.

extras.note: Sends the got_request_exception signal and logs the exception before producing the 500 response.
PROPAGATE_EXCEPTIONS unset means propagate when testing or debug is enabled.

uncertainties: Whether got_request_exception.send can itself raise (signal receivers are invoked synchronously) is not guarded here.

units.explain: Logs the exception via self.logger.error with a message containing the request path and method ('Exception on <path> [<method>]') and exc_info passed to the logging call for the traceback. Assumes an active request in ctx; ctx.request.path/method are read directly.
units.summary: Log the current exception with request path and method via the app logger.

units.explain: Matches the request to a view and invokes it. If req.routing_exception is set, passes it to raise_routing_exception (which re-raises it, possibly transformed in debug). Reads req.url_rule (typed as Rule); if the rule allows automatic options and the method is OPTIONS, returns make_default_options_response(ctx). Otherwise calls the view function self.view_functions[rule.endpoint] with req.view_args as kwargs, through ensure_sync so async views work. Unknown endpoints (missing from view_functions) would raise KeyError; not guarded. Returns the raw view return value, which need not be a Response.
units.summary: Dispatch the request to its view function, handling routing exceptions and automatic OPTIONS.
uncertainties: url_rule/view_args being non-None relies on routing having matched; the type: ignore comments acknowledge this.

units.explain: Placeholder id in inventory refers to the full-dispatch pipeline below.
units.summary: Pipeline: first-request flag and deprecation warning, request_started signal, preprocess/dispatch, exception conversion, finalization.

units.explain: Runs the full request cycle. If this is not the first request handled and self.should_ignore_error is defined (not None), warns DeprecationWarning that should_ignore_error is deprecated (to be removed in Flask 3.3). Sets self._got_first_request = True unconditionally. Then: sends request_started (with ensure_sync as async wrapper), runs preprocess_request(ctx); if it returned None, runs dispatch_request(ctx). Any Exception raised in that block is converted via handle_user_exception(ctx, e). Finally returns finalize_request(ctx, rv), which builds the response and runs after-request functions. Only Exception (not BaseException) is caught here.
units.summary: First-request bookkeeping, preprocess and dispatch the request, convert exceptions, and finalize into a response.

extras.note: Sets self._got_first_request = True before dispatch, enabling first-request-only warnings/behavior.

uncertainties: should_ignore_error is referenced via the sansio base; its definition/None-ness is external.

units.explain: Turns a view/error-handler return value into a Response: make_response(rv), then process_response(ctx, response) and the request_finished signal inside a try. If those raise: when from_error_handler is False the exception propagates; when True (error path), the exception is logged with self.logger.exception and the (possibly partially processed) response is returned. Returns the final Response.
units.summary: Convert a view return value into a response, run after-request processing, and log failures on the error path.

extras.note: Called with from_error_handler=True by handle_exception, so after-request failures are logged instead of raised.

units.explain: Builds the automatic OPTIONS response: an empty self.response_class() whose Allow header is set to the allowed methods reported by ctx.url_adapter.allowed_methods() (url_adapter assumed present; the type: ignore notes the possibility of None). Override point for changing automatic OPTIONS behavior.
units.summary: Return an empty response whose Allow header lists the route's allowed methods.
uncertainties: Behavior when ctx has no url_adapter (AttributeError from None) is not guarded.

units.explain: Adapts a callable for synchronous WSGI invocation: coroutine functions (per inspect.iscoroutinefunction) are wrapped via async_to_sync; everything else is returned unchanged. Override point for custom async handling.
units.summary: Return async functions wrapped for sync calling; pass other callables through unchanged.

units.explain: Converts a coroutine function into a sync callable using asgiref.sync.async_to_sync, imported lazily. If asgiref is not installed, raises RuntimeError('Install Flask with the 'async' extra ...') with the ImportError suppressed (from None). Returns the asgiref wrapper; the caller invokes the result to run the coroutine to completion.
units.summary: Wrap a coroutine function with asgiref's async_to_sync, raising RuntimeError if asgiref is missing.

extras.note: Raises RuntimeError when the asgiref dependency is absent; the original ImportError is chained off (None).

uncertainties: Precise event-loop behavior of the asgiref wrapper is library-defined.

units.explain: Builds a URL for an endpoint. Adapter selection: if an app context is active and has a request, uses ctx.url_adapter and the current blueprint; an endpoint starting with '.' is made relative to the active blueprint (or the leading dot is stripped when there is none), and URLs default to internal unless _scheme forces external (_external = _scheme is not None). Outside a request, uses the app context's url_adapter if an app context is active, otherwise builds one via create_url_adapter(None); if no adapter is available (no SERVER_NAME), raises RuntimeError explaining the configuration needed, and URLs default to external. Validates that _scheme requires _external=True (ValueError otherwise). Calls self.inject_url_defaults(endpoint, values), then url_adapter.build(endpoint, values, method=_method, url_scheme=_scheme, force_external=_external). On BuildError, merges _anchor/_method/_scheme/_external into values and delegates to self.handle_url_build_error(error, endpoint, values); if that returns a string it is returned, otherwise the BuildError propagates per the sansio method. A non-None _anchor is URL-quoted with a permissive safe set and appended as '#anchor'.
units.summary: Build a URL for an endpoint using the request or app URL adapter, with blueprint-relative endpoints and build-error handling.

extras.note: Raises RuntimeError when building URLs outside a request without SERVER_NAME; ValueError when _scheme is given with _external=False.

uncertainties: Whether handle_url_build_error always raises or may return is determined by the sansio implementation, not this file.

units.explain: Coerces a view return value into self.response_class. Tuple unpacking: 3-tuples are (body, status, headers); 2-tuples are (body, headers) when the second element is a Headers/dict/tuple/list, else (body, status); other lengths raise TypeError. A None body raises TypeError naming the endpoint from the request proxy. Non-response bodies: str/bytes/bytearray/iterator become response_class(rv, status=status, headers=headers) with status/headers consumed there; dict/list become self.json.response(rv) (JSON response; status/headers from tuple unpacking are not applied in this branch); a werkzeug BaseResponse or any callable is coerced via response_class.force_type(rv, request.environ) — this requires an active request context, and a TypeError there is re-raised as a new TypeError with appended guidance and the original traceback. Anything else raises TypeError listing accepted types. Afterwards an unpacked status is applied (string sets rv.status, otherwise rv.status_code) and unpacked headers update rv.headers. Returns the Response.
units.summary: Convert any supported view return value (body, tuples, dict/list JSON, WSGI callable, Response) into a Response.

relations.basis: self.json.response(rv) — two candidate provider implementations; exact target unresolved

extras.note: Raises TypeError for None returns, malformed tuples, and unsupported return types; coerces foreign Responses or WSGI callables via force_type.
In the dict/list JSON branch, tuple-supplied status/headers are not applied to the JSON response.

uncertainties: Whether self.json.response consumes or should consume tuple status/headers is defined in flask.json.provider and not visible here.
The graph shows two candidate implementations of response() (JSONProvider / DefaultJSONProvider); which one runs depends on the configured json provider.

units.explain: Pre-dispatch hooks. Runs url_value_preprocessors for None (app-level) and the request's blueprints in reverse order, calling each with (req.endpoint, req.view_args). Then runs before_request_funcs for the same names, each through ensure_sync; the first non-None return value short-circuits and is returned (it becomes the response value, skipping the view). Returns None when all before-request functions return None. URL value preprocessors cannot short-circuit.
units.summary: Run URL value preprocessors and before_request functions; a non-None before_request return short-circuits dispatch.

units.explain: Post-dispatch hooks, in reverse registration order. First runs ctx._after_request_functions (deferred, e.g. from streaming within the request), then after_request_funcs for each of the request's blueprints then None (app-level), each through ensure_sync, chaining the response through each function's return. Finally, if the session is not a null session (session_interface.is_null_session(ctx._get_session())), saves it via session_interface.save_session(self, session, response). Returns the final response.
units.summary: Run after_request functions in reverse order and save the non-null session onto the response.
uncertainties: Behavior of _after_request_functions population is defined in flask.ctx.

units.explain: Runs request teardown before the request context pops (invoked by AppContext.pop). Iterates the request's blueprints then None; for each name with registered teardown_request_funcs, runs each function in reverse registration order with exc, inside a _CollectErrors context so an error in one callback does not stop later callbacks. Then sends the request_tearing_down signal (with exc) under the same collector, and finally collect_errors.raise_any('Errors during request teardown'), which re-raises the collected errors if any occurred (behavior of the helpers._CollectErrors helper).
units.summary: Run teardown_request functions and the request_tearing_down signal, collecting errors instead of stopping at the first.

relations.basis: docstring and graph: called by AppContext.pop

uncertainties: Exact raise semantics (single exception vs ExceptionGroup) of _CollectErrors.raise_any are defined in flask.helpers, not proven here.

units.explain: Runs app teardown before the app context pops (invoked by AppContext.pop). Runs teardown_appcontext_funcs in reverse order with exc under _CollectErrors, then sends appcontext_tearing_down (with exc) under the collector, then raises collected errors via collect_errors.raise_any('Errors during app teardown'). As with do_teardown_request, all callbacks run even if earlier ones raise.
units.summary: Run teardown_appcontext functions and the appcontext_tearing_down signal, collecting errors across callbacks.

relations.basis: docstring and graph: called by AppContext.pop

uncertainties: raise_any failure shape is defined in flask.helpers.

units.explain: Creates and returns a new AppContext(self); nothing is pushed by this method itself — pushing happens via the context manager or ctx.push(), which makes current_app and g available. Used directly for setup/testing outside request handling or CLI commands.
units.summary: Create (but do not push) an AppContext for this application.

units.explain: Creates an AppContext carrying a request built from the given WSGI environment via AppContext.from_environ(self, environ). Intended for internal use; the docs steer external code to test_request_context because a valid environ is nontrivial. Pushing the result makes request, session, g, and current_app available.
units.summary: Create an AppContext with a request built from a WSGI environment.
uncertainties: from_environ's request construction and session handling are defined in flask.ctx.

units.explain: Builds a WSGI environ for testing: constructs flask.testing.EnvironBuilder(self, *args, **kwargs) (which applies app defaults like PREFERRED_URL_SCHEME and SERVER_NAME), calls builder.get_environ() inside try/finally so builder.close() always runs, then returns self.request_context(environ). Accepts the same arguments as werkzeug.test.EnvironBuilder; a json kwarg is serialized and defaults content_type to application/json (per EnvironBuilder).
units.summary: Create a request-bearing AppContext from EnvironBuilder arguments for testing.
uncertainties: get_environ failure modes are Werkzeug/testing-defined.

units.explain: The actual WSGI application (kept separate from __call__ so middleware can wrap it without losing the app object). Creates ctx = request_context(environ), pushes it, and runs full_dispatch_request(ctx). On Exception, records error and produces handle_exception(ctx, e); on BaseException (bare except), records error and re-raises. Returns response(environ, start_response) — the JSON provider's response method supplies this callable for the final WSGI invocation. The finally block always: preserves the context for the Werkzeug debugger if environ contains 'werkzeug.debug.preserve_context'; clears the recorded error if should_ignore_error is defined and returns truthy for it; and calls ctx.pop(error), which runs request/app teardown with the error (or None if ignored/absent). Teardown therefore runs even on unhandled errors.
units.summary: WSGI entry pipeline: push request context, dispatch, convert errors, return response, always pop context with teardown.
